intro: The true hill stations nearest Kolkata are in the far north of West Bengal: Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Kurseong and Mirik, with Sikkim just beyond. They are reached by an overnight train to New Jalpaiguri or a short flight to Bagdogra, followed by three hours or so by road.

For a shorter break, the low hills and plateaus of Purulia (Ajodhya Hills), Jharkhand (Ghatshila, Netarhat) and the forests of Jhargram offer greenery, waterfalls and cooler evenings in winter, though they are not hill stations in the Himalayan sense.
quickAnswer: The nearest hill stations to Kolkata are in the Darjeeling hills: Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Kurseong and Mirik, about 560 km away by overnight train to New Jalpaiguri or a flight to Bagdogra, then around three hours by road. Sikkim is a few hours further. For a shorter break, Ajodhya Hills in Purulia, Ghatshila and Netarhat in Jharkhand, and Jhargram's forests are closer.
takeaways: Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Kurseong and Mirik are the nearest true hill stations.
Take an overnight train to New Jalpaiguri, or fly to Bagdogra.
Four to five days suits the Darjeeling hills; a week adds Sikkim.
Ajodhya Hills, Ghatshila and Jhargram make shorter plateau and forest breaks.
Book early for the Puja holidays and summer vacation.

sections.heading: When to go
list: March to May: popular summer escape to the Darjeeling hills; book early.
October to December: the clearest mountain views, and the Puja holidays.
June to September: monsoon rain and landslides in the hills.
October to March: the best time for the closer plateau breaks.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: In Darjeeling, stay near Chowrasta and the Mall for walkability, or on a tea estate below town for quiet. Kalimpong and Kurseong have heritage hotels and homestays. For Ajodhya Hills, Ghatshila and Jhargram, stays are simpler, including state and forest department lodges; book ahead for winter weekends.

sections.heading: Getting there
paras: Several overnight trains run from Kolkata's Sealdah and Howrah stations to New Jalpaiguri, and there are frequent flights to Bagdogra. From either, shared jeeps and taxis take about three hours to Darjeeling and a little less to Kalimpong, Kurseong and Mirik. For Ajodhya Hills, trains run to Purulia; Ghatshila and Jhargram are on the Howrah to Tatanagar line.

safety: Drive times are approximate and depend on traffic, weather and road works; weekend traffic on hill roads can double them. Avoid driving on mountain roads after dark.
Check weather and road updates before leaving, especially in the monsoon.
Book stays early for long weekends.

faqs.q: Which is the nearest hill station to Kolkata?
faqs.a: The Darjeeling hills (Darjeeling, Kurseong, Mirik and Kalimpong) are the nearest true hill stations, reached by overnight train or a flight to Bagdogra.

faqs.q: Can I visit Darjeeling for a weekend from Kolkata?
faqs.a: It is possible with an overnight train both ways, but four days is more comfortable.

faqs.q: Are there hills closer to Kolkata?
faqs.a: Ajodhya Hills in Purulia, Ghatshila, Jhargram and Netarhat are closer, low-hill and forest breaks.

faqs.q: How do I get from Kolkata to Darjeeling?
faqs.a: An overnight train to New Jalpaiguri or a flight to Bagdogra, then about three hours by road.

faqs.q: When should I visit the Darjeeling hills from Kolkata?
faqs.a: March to May and October to December; book early for the Puja holidays.

faqs.q: Is Mirik worth a day trip?
faqs.a: Yes, for its lake and tea gardens; it combines well with Kurseong on the drive up or down.
